meta.title: Incoming local-file import and recovery lifecycle

cards.title: Linked lifecycle scope
items: Import and recovery scope starts at an already staged item; the initial marker denotes entry to this view, not item creation. Preparation, pre-import cancellation and no-receipt retry routes remain in the linked preparation and review diagram. Cancelled is the same shared persisted status.
The two views partition the original sixteen transitions without changing transition labels, notes, variants or direction. Shared states retain their original meaning and committed source evidence.

cards.title: Transition gates
items: Claim is FIFO and requires an active queue and no preparing or importing item. Fenced copy requires the matching attempt and stage identity without cancellation.
Guarded plan application requires fresh Desktop protection, a History operation and checked exact review. Reconcile to imported requires matching completed History and a persisted positive Track ID.
Owner recovery requeues abandoned preparation without cancellation; settle cancel means completion or abandoned-preparation recovery observes requested cancellation.

Retry fresh and reuse copy require no History receipt. Fresh means no retained content hash; reuse copy requires a retained content hash. Effective Undo may cancel importing before receipt completion; reversing Undo requires the complete original receipt. Neither reconciliation path resubmits an import.

cards.title: Suspension is separate control state
items: QueueControl pauses claims and reviewed imports without inventing an item status.
Missing, pending, failed or incomplete import evidence pauses the queue for recovery unless effective Undo establishes cancellation; importing does not automatically become retryable.
Manual and restored suspension require explicit Resume. Resume reconciles import receipts before clearing suspension; opening a service preserves it.
Reconciliation never submits collection writes. Explicit review and apply own import consent.

cards.title: Service and request lifetimes
items: An API-owned library service resumes ownership and eligible preparation for enrolled queues independently of HTTP requests, preserving suspension.
Cancelling a Process waiter leaves background preparation owned by the service.
Service Close cancels and joins preparation before closing queue storage; replacement obtains this ownership before scheduler and History locks.

cards.title: Independent publication and recovery
items: Durable import intent precedes collection changes; the exact Track receipt precedes the caller's After snapshot.
Engine writes, intake receipts and History completion are separate publications. Incomplete evidence retains recovery requirements unless effective Undo establishes cancellation.
Staged files remain available until explicit cleanup. Quiet time is an observation heuristic, not proof that a source writer has finished.

cards.title: Coherent intake observation
items: Existing retained import receipts are observed while holding the native History owner before the intake worker owner, matching import lock order. A live History publisher is waited for cancellably rather than reported as a recovery failure.

The observer rereads the current ImportIntent tuple (item_id, history_id and persisted track_id receipt) and conditionally updates matching Item state after both owners are held. Resume retains this coherent observation boundary until reconciliation succeeds and suspension is cleared. Engine publication, queue receipts and History completion remain independent commits.

A queue without retained import intents does not enroll or wait on History merely to prepare sources. Missing History is identified before observation and checked again under the worker owner; unresolved missing or incomplete evidence still requires recovery.
Service shutdown cancels an initial History wait and joins the worker without publishing successful initial readiness or recording cancellation as a worker failure.

Import review opens its intake service before entering the shared Smartlist-safe read boundary. Only its database review callback, inside Service.Use, takes that read lease. At the original 6c8135c evidence revision, a live publisher or pending repair refused review; current reader ownership is described in the Cancellable collection reads supplement below; explicit import remains in the existing Desktop-protected History publication path.

Committed evidence: 6c8135c64da17554f2ff2aa6dbac05cf6270529c; internal/history/observe_entries.go:20–56; internal/intake/import.go:140–219; internal/intake/control.go:24–30; internal/intake/service.go:129–189; internal/api/intake.go:155–182. Historical diagram pins remain unchanged.

cards.title: Cancellable collection reads
items: Public Smartlist-safe collection reads, including intake import review, wait cancellably for an existing History publisher. Completed import receipt reconciliation therefore does not make an immediate collection refresh fail merely because it briefly retains History.

A pending per-library read owner is published before native acquisition. The process-global readers mutex is released during the native wait, so unrelated libraries and existing readers can make progress. Overlapping readers share one retained native lease.

Each waiting reader can cancel independently. A cancelled first acquirer removes its pending owner and wakes surviving waiters to retry. Once acquired, the native lease is detached from that first reader context and remains until its last reader releases it.

Pending repair detected before acquisition refuses immediately; pending repair is checked again after acquisition before any observation. Reads do not recover or apply repair. Private History List and mutation acquisition retain fail-fast behavior; Desktop protection, snapshots and Undo publication remain unchanged.

Source evidence: 76d507cd514fc04c15bff17f69eba37bb3b591ce; internal/history/history.go:73–99; internal/history/smartlist_read_lock.go:24–83; internal/history/smartlist_observe.go; internal/history/smartlist_barrier.go:54–58. Behavioral evidence: internal/history/smartlist_read_wait_test.go and internal/api/intake_review_read_test.go; the immediate post-import GET is covered by internal/api/intake_import_test.go. Historical source pins remain unchanged.

cards.title: Readable-audio admission before collection installation
items: Collection admission requires both an audio stream and a decoded audio frame from native ffprobe. Missing ffprobe fails closed; malformed output, an absent audio stream or a stream without decoded frames is refused. The first interval is relative to the initial timestamp and does not certify the entire file.

AddTrack checks before directory creation, source moves and collection writes. Ordinary staging import checks before audio installation; intake review uses the same requirement before returning a consent token. Discovery and source-preserving staging alone do not claim collection eligibility.

Cancellation during the final staged import item returns the partial imported report with context cancellation before classifying that item as failed. Existing public job handling retains partial results and reports cancellation.

Source evidence: 6d1b89aec69fef14dfbd76a43c890d5fa9ded0c4; internal/track/track.go:44–83,117–129; internal/staging/import.go:48–83,101–120; internal/intake/import.go:33–53; internal/api/jobs.go:155–174. No whole-file integrity or platform qualification is implied.

cards.title: Supplemental evidence scope
items: Supplemental source revisions: refusal-preserving Undo 494689f197e1afcaaae6ba1090159165b7953c1a; readable-audio admission 6d1b89aec69fef14dfbd76a43c890d5fa9ded0c4; cancellable collection reads 76d507cd514fc04c15bff17f69eba37bb3b591ce; watched-folder ownership 05102c1cc0c4b1db00826dc007753b544162e79b. Historical repository pins and cards retain their original scope. Source evidence does not establish renderer checks, whole-file audio integrity or native-platform qualification.

cards.title: Native shared readers and exclusive publishers
items: ReadSmartlistSafe and ReadSmartlistProjection retain a native shared History lease for an enrolled library. Readers in separate processes can overlap; readers in one process share a reference-counted owner. The last reader releases that owner, independently of the first reader’s cancellation.

History publication takes an exclusive lease on the same empty lock database. The lock database must be an empty regular file using a rollback journal. Native acquisition remains cancellable where the caller requests waiting; mutating History operations keep their fail-fast policy.

ObserveEntries retains exclusive ownership while handing History entries to intake reconciliation. It is not the shared read lease. Intake preparation/import states and their recovery transitions do not change.

Committed source evidence d3de75b98ba479484d49b0779087f080cb641820: internal/history/smartlist_read_lock.go:26–113; internal/history/history.go:73–101; internal/history/history_lock.go:13–58; internal/history/observe_entries.go:18–58. Historical source pins and existing graph topology remain unchanged.
